subject: ShopNow pilot: TTFT assumptions, streaming cadence, and pilot kickoff
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Harper Lewis <harper@shopnow.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: ShopNow pilot: TTFT assumptions, streaming cadence, and pilot kickoff

Hi Harper — great conversation today. Thanks for walking us through ShopNow's storefront assistant priorities. Quick recap so we have aligned expectations going into the pilot: 

Summary of ShopNow goals
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): target p50 <= 200ms, p95 <= 400ms for live user-facing sessions.
- Streaming behavior: prefer server-sent events (SSE) for browser clients; fallback WebSocket only if SSE blocked.
- Chunk cadence: want small chunks every ~200–350ms to show progressive typing for UX.
- Concurrency/throughput: planning for steady-state 60 concurrent active sessions during peak, spike up to 180 concurrent sessions for promos. Median response payload ~180–350 tokens; occasional long responses up to ~900 tokens.
- Degradation policy: graceful fallback to non-streaming (single response) if streaming cannot meet TTFT SLA; must detect and surface to client within 500ms.

Immediate asks from Redwood
1) Please confirm the peak concurrency assumptions above (60 steady, 180 spike) and typical session lengths.
2) Share a 24h sample traffic dump (anonymized) and 3 representative prompt payloads we can use for a load benchmark.
3) Any platform constraints: CORS, customers behind corporate proxies, or WAFs that might block SSE?

Next steps / timeline
- Redwood to run a scoped benchmark against a dedicated test environment (we'll provision a small sandbox dedicated capacity) using your sample payloads — estimate 3 business days after we get payloads.
- Post-benchmark we’ll share: a) measured TTFT at p50/p95, b) recommended batching and chunking cadence, c) fallback behavior and SLO docs.
- Pilot kickoff meeting: propose Wed 7/7 10:00–10:45am PT to review SOW and runbook.

Attachments: shopnow-traffic-dashboard.csv (for your reference), pilot-sow-draft.pdf (initial SOW & scope), ttft-payloads-PRD.jsonl (placeholder payloads from our side).

Thanks — Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0194
From: Harper Lewis <harper@shopnow.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@shopnow.io>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ShopNow pilot: TTFT assumptions, streaming cadence, and pilot kickoff

Thanks, Soojin — that captures the call cleanly. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Concurrency: 60 steady is correct for baseline. Spikes historically top out closer to 220 concurrent active sessions on big promo days; we can provision for 250 for safety during the pilot.
- Session length: median 3.8 minutes; average message tokens ~240.
- SSE constraints: most browsers work fine but our corporate customers sometimes route traffic through a proxy that terminates long-lived SSE; we can provide a list of customers that saw issues.

We attached a 24h anonymized traffic CSV (shopnow-traffic-dashboard.csv). We'll also export three representative prompts as you requested — sending as a Drive link in a separate email.

Pilot planning: Wed 7/7 10:00 PT works for Harper and Alex. Can you also include an agenda with bench goals?

Also: on fallback behavior, we'd prefer a client-visible flag that indicates 'stream degraded' so we can switch to a compact UI mode.

Best,
Harper
Head of Product — ShopNow
harper@shopnow.io
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: ShopNow pilot: TTFT assumptions, streaming cadence, and pilot kickoff

Looping Ben in (internal QA + benchmarks owner). Action items for us: 
- Scope test environment: replicate 250 concurrent sessions with median token size 240 and a 900-token tail. Run two ramp profiles: steady-state 60 and spike to 250 for 10 minutes. 
- Measure: p50/p95 TTFT, p50/p95 token-emit cadence, % of connections that required fallback, CPU/GPU utilization, and memory/KV cache hit rates.
- Produce a one-page bench result summary and a 2–3 slide recommended config (batching, quantization profile, and chunk pacing).

I will assemble a short runbook and ping infra to provision a sandbox with isolation and mock user agents to simulate SSE and WebSocket clients. Also recommend we include a client-side telemetry snippet so ShopNow can flag 'stream degraded' events as Harper requested.

Tagging Monica to prepare the sample payload bundle and a short security checklist for the pilot environment.

-Ben

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Harper Lewis <harper@shopnow.io>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ShopNow pilot: TTFT assumptions, streaming cadence, and pilot kickoff

Hi Harper — dropping the payloads and a brief security note. Links: 
- Prompts & payloads (anonymized): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d-shopnow-pilot (will contain ttft-payloads-PRD.jsonl and a README).
- Security checklist (summary): minimal PII in payloads, all samples hashed; TLS enforced; keys rotated for the sandbox; logging retention set to 30 days for pilot.

Attached: ttft-payloads-PRD.jsonl (sample prompts), pilot-sow-draft.pdf (SOW draft; please review any compliance items), shopnow-traffic-dashboard.csv (already provided by ShopNow).

Questions for ShopNow: 
1) For the 250-concurrency spike, do you prefer we prioritize TTFT p95 at the cost of throughput, or maintain throughput and allow a small TTFT degradation? Give us your preference and we’ll tune accordingly.
2) Can ShopNow surface client-side events when SSE drops to help us correlate server logs? Harper mentioned they can, but we need the event names/fields.

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Harper Lewis <harper@shopnow.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ShopNow pilot: TTFT assumptions, streaming cadence, and pilot kickoff

Thanks team — we reviewed the materials. Quick answers: 
1) For 250-concurrency spikes, prioritize TTFT p95. UX is paramount during promos — if you need to trade throughput for lower TTFT, do it.
2) We'll add a client telemetry event: shopnow.stream.status with fields {session_id, status: [ok,degraded,closed], reason}. We’ll share the telemetry spec by EOD Monday.

Confirming Wed 7/7 10:00 PT for kickoff. Agenda request: 
- Bench goals & pass/fail criteria (Ben)
- Pilot SOW highlights and security items (Monica)
- Client telemetry and fallback handling (Harper)
- Next: timeline for production rollout if bench passes (Soojin)

Harper
Head of Product — ShopNow
harper@shopnow.io
